supersedes_public_geometry: The degree-two ring remains only a small-graph/throughput fixture and no longer represents the public lattice-level artifact.
geometries: Lab 002 square lattice with open rough left/right boundaries and smooth transverse boundaries
Lab 002 honeycomb lattice with open rough left/right boundaries and armchair-smooth transverse boundaries
frozen_effect: Delta r_a=P(e_a=1|m,R)-P(e_a=1|m), red positive, blue negative, width proportional to magnitude.
acceptance_gates: Square and honeycomb graph payloads reproduce the canonical Lab 002 vertex, edge, detector, boundary-side, and logical-cut data.
All retained edges touch one or two detector factors and hard corrections reproduce m on detector rows.
U(1), SU(2), and SU(3) local fusion distributions normalize for every detector degree exercised by both geometries.
The two posterior arms use the same physical error, m record, prior, schedule, and full-irrep sample.
The artifact exposes BP convergence, iterations, and residual rather than implying that convergence or exactness is guaranteed on short loops.
The exact Lab Results page visibly renders both geometries, rough boundaries, all four layers, and the signed R effect.
The ring is described only as an exact-enumeration and throughput fixture in current report, plan, metadata, and Wiki.
sampling: Interactive fixed-seed explanatory samples only; no finite-size performance or threshold sampling is authorized by this transition.
stop_rule: Fail closed if either 2D geometry, syndrome fidelity, fusion normalization, paired-record identity, convergence diagnostics, or the exact rendered surface fails.
